catalog.text:
Ner could borrow the owl queen's night sight for one season by surrendering the memory of a face. The offer would help her find a lost flock tonight. Her brother stood beside her holding the empty feed bag. The queen had not named whose face would be taken.

A feather caught on the feed bag's seam.

catalog.text:
At the conservatory dinner, Ada's rival Florian found her packing the cheaper violin into the prize case. The award paid tuition but required a tour she could not afford to join. Florian had not seen her contract. Their teachers were making toasts in the next room.

Rosin whitened the velvet lining.

catalog.text:
Bakers Lio and Hana prepare one wedding cake together. Lio wants to close the shop for their first date; Hana must keep it open to cover her apprentice's wages. Neither has agreed to a closing time. The wedding delivery is fixed for four.

The apprentice, Soli, is paid weekly and has already bought supplies for the wedding cake. Hana controls that wage account; Lio controls the delivery van booking. The van must be returned at six. Their customer has approved the cake design, so design changes cannot solve the scheduling conflict without a new conversation. The shop can operate with either baker present, but the glaze needs two people for a brief lift. They have promised the apprentice an uninterrupted lunch break. Lio interprets Hana's refusal as reluctance about the date; Hana has only spoken about wages. Neither interpretation has been tested in conversation. The next scene occurs while the glaze cools, before the four o'clock delivery. A workable compromise is possible, but none is yet canon.

Mara keeps the harbor archive. Ilan repairs its flooded shelves. At noon Mara accuses Ilan of selling a brass ledger, but she has no evidence. Ilan says he moved it above the tide line. Mara cannot open the upper room because only the retired keeper has its key. A red scarf hangs on a chair; nobody refers to it again. The chapter ends before anyone enters the upper room.

In this region, places can remember promises spoken inside them. a tidal archive has begun repeating a fragment of an old vow after dark. Mara and Ilan do not know whose promise it was or whether it concerns them.

Oren is a ferry clerk. Leda boards with an unsigned ticket and asks him not to announce her destination. Oren thinks she is fleeing a creditor, but she has not told him why she is traveling. The ferry will stop at Bell Quay before continuing to the island. Only the captain knows the revised sailing time. A chipped blue plate rolls under a bench. Leda waits by the gangway while Oren decides whether to call the captain.

Oren has received a letter from an old love who wants to meet again. Leda knows about the invitation but has not read the letter. A possible reunion complicates Oren's feelings about remaining at a night ferry; no decision has been made.
